title: 2025年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2025年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with her hairdresser(理发师) about retirement plans. The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to. The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money.

P2 Both scenarios(情况) are contributing to a big increase in the number of people in the U.S. working into their 70s. Over the past 20 years, the share of Americans working in their 70s has risen from less than 10% to nearly 15%.

P3 In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement. The decline of manufacturing and the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations also has contributed to the trend, says Abraham, who researches work and retirement decisions of older Americans.

P4 "Which matters more depends on what your history up until that point has been in the type of work you're doing," Abraham says.

P5 The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category. The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018. For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%.

P6 Martin Neil Baily, an economist who is leading a research project on retirement security, notes that quitting a career can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness, particularly for men. He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons. They're also more likely to be in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more.

P7 Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons.

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about the economics professor and her hairdresser?
options: They differ in their reasons for continuing to work.
They are both committed to working into their 70s.
They are happy about their current financial situation.
They hold different views about postponing retirement.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn from the passage about the economics professor and her hairdresser 锁定两位具体人物，要在原文里抓他们各自的具体说法，属于事实型细节题。 51. What do we learn from the passage about the economics professor and her hairdresser? A) They differ in their reasons for continuing to work. B) They are both committed to working into their 70s. C) They are happy about their current financial situation. D) They hold different views about postponing retirement.

【拆句】句子主干是 What do we learn from the passage about ...，about 引出涉及的对象；并 列结构 the economics professor and her hairdresser 由 and 连接两个名词短语，无从 句、无否定，结构平直无陷阱。

【定位】The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to. The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money. 经济学家说她打算继续工作，因为她想这样做。理发师也同意继续工作，但理由不同：她需 要钱。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason ↔ They differ in their reasons for continuing to work 预判强调 "两人继续工作的理由不同"，A 项 They differ in their reasons for continuing to work 恰好对此点 100% 命中，无引申无超纲，可直接锁定。 B) 答非所问 B 项 They are both committed to working into their 70s 把题目焦点偏到 "是否都坚 持工作到 70 多岁"，但题目问的是 "对照两人有何不同"，不是问共同点。 C) 无中生有 C 项 They are happy about their current financial situation 说两人都对当前财务状 况满意，但理发师明确说 She needs the money，怎么也谈不上 happy。 D) 偷换概念 D 项 They hold different views about postponing retirement 似乎与 A 相近，但 different views about postponing retirement 意为 "在是否推迟退休这件事上观点不 同"，而原文里两人都决定继续工作，差异在理由而不在观点。 人们推迟退休的原因之一是什么? A) 越来越多的人转向了智力挑战性较低的工作。 B) 私营部门适合老年人的工作岗位数量增加了。 C) 多年来,按购买力计算的工资增长率有所放缓。 D) 职场中越来越多的人发现难以依靠传统养老金。

questions.q: What is one of the reasons for people to delay retirement?
options: More and more people have switched to less intellectually challenging jobs.
The number of jobs suitable for older people has increased in the private sector.
The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years.
More and more people in the workplace find it hard to rely on traditional pensions.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is one of the reasons for people to delay retirement 询问具体原因，要在原 文清单里点对清单项，属典型细节题。

【拆句】主干 What is one of the reasons，后接介词短语 for people to delay retirement 作后置 定语；for 引导原因方向，不定式 to delay 表逻辑动作，结构清晰，无难点。 52. What is one of the reasons for people to delay retirement? A) More and more people have switched to less intellectually challenging jobs. B) The number of jobs suitable for older people has increased in the private sector. C) The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years. D) More and more people in the workplace find it hard to rely on traditional pensions.

【定位】In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement. 除了人们更健康、寿命更长之外，经济学家说，多重经济因素的叠加——例如实际工资多年 增长缓慢，以及私人部门远离传统养老金——是人们延迟退休的部分原因。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文说 the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations——是 "从事劳动强度小的职业的人变多"，A 项 less intellectually challenging jobs 偷换为 "智力上挑战较小的工作"，labor-intensive（体力密集）与 intellectually challenging（智力挑战）不是一回事。 B) 无中生有 B 项 The number of jobs suitable for older people has increased in the private sector 说私人部门里适合老年人的岗位增多，但原文 a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector 谈的是养老金机制远离传统模式，并未谈岗位数量的 变化。 C) ✓ 正确 years of slow rise in real wages ↔ The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years 预判锁定 "实际工资多年涨得慢"，C 项 The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years 把同一信息用购买力的角度表达，是 教科书式同义替换。 D) 偷换概念 原文 a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector 是 "私人部门正在 远离传统养老金"——指制度变化；D 项 find it hard to rely on traditional pensions 偷换成 "人们觉得难以依赖传统养老金"——指主观感受。两者方向虽近，但原文从未谈 及人们的主观难度感。 人们推迟退休的总体趋势是什么? A) 收入越高,他们越有可能倾向于推迟退休。 B) 工作满意度更高的人往往比满意度较低的人退休得更晚。 C) 留在劳动力市场直到70多岁的男性可能多于女性。 D) 教育水平越高,他们越有可能推迟退休。

questions.q: What is the general trend in people delaying retirement?
options: The higher their earnings, the more likely they are tempted to delay retirement.
Those who have more job satisfaction tend to retire later than those who have less.
More men than women are likely to stay in the labor force until their late seventies.
The higher their educational level, the more likely they are to delay retirement.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is the general trend in people delaying retirement 询问的是原文里已经写明 的整体规律，去找总括句即可，不需越级推断。

【拆句】主干 What is the general trend，介词短语 in people delaying retirement 中 people delaying retirement 是 in 的复合宾语（动名词短语带逻辑主语），结构平直、无从句。

【定位】The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category. The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018. For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%. 这一整体趋势影响着所有学历层次的美国人，尽管各类别的比例有所不同。拥有本科学历、 且仍在 70 多岁工作的美国人比例在 2018 年达到近 20%；高中及以下学历者比例约 10%；有部分大学经历者居中，约 15%。

【选项】A) 无中生有 A 项 The higher their earnings, the more likely they are tempted to delay retirement 把维度换成 earnings（收入），原文 all different levels of educational attainment 谈的是学历，没有任何收入分层数据。 B) 张冠李戴 B 项 Those who have more job satisfaction tend to retire later than those who have less 谈职业满意度的影响，但本段只有学历分层数据，没有关于 job satisfaction 的对比；此话题虽在第 6 段简短出现，与 "general trend" 不是同一议题。 C) 张冠李戴 C 项 More men than women are likely to stay in the labor force until their late seventies 涉及性别差异，原文虽然第 6 段提到 particularly for men，但那是讲孤独 感、不是 general trend 数据；本段从未做性别对比。 D) ✓ 正确 The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% ↔The higher their educational level, the more likely they are to delay retirement 预判出 "学历越高，延迟退休比例越高"，D 项 The higher their educational level, the more likely they are to delay retirement 正是这一规律的语句化，无遗漏无超纲。 根据一位经济学家的说法,受过大学教育的工人推迟退休的主要原因是什么? A) 享有财务保障。 B) 保持社交联系。 C) 在专业方面做出更多贡献。 D) 增加社会保障金支付。 54. What is the chief reason for college-educated workers delaying retirement according to an economist? A) Enjoying financial security. B) Staying connected socially. C) Contributing more professionally. D) Increasing social security payments.

questions.q: What is the chief reason for college-educated workers delaying retirement according to an economist?
options: Enjoying financial security.
Staying connected socially.
Contributing more professionally.
Increasing social security payments.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is the chief reason for college-educated workers delaying retirement 询问 原文中经济学家明确给出的主因，按细节题处理即可。

【拆句】主干 What is the chief reason，介词短语 for college-educated workers delaying retirement 作后置定语，分词 delaying 修饰 workers 表正在延迟；末尾 according to an economist 是插入限定信息源，结构清晰。

【定位】He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons. 他指出，许多受过大学教育的劳动者选择继续留在劳动力市场，更多是出于社交方面的好 处，而不是经济原因。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 A 项 Enjoying financial security 把主因说成 "享受经济保障"，但原文明确 more for social benefits than for financial reasons —— financial 恰恰是被否定的次要原因， A 项正好反向。 B) ✓ 正确 more for social benefits than for financial reasons ↔Staying connected socially 预判抓 social benefits，B 项 Staying connected socially 正面命中；其余选项均与 social 无直接对应，可一眼锁定。 C) 过度推断 C 项 Contributing more professionally 说 "在专业上贡献更多"，原文 in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more 只说他们多从事专业职业、 并享受工作，并未提 "为了贡献更多" 才不退休。 D) 无中生有 D 项 Increasing social security payments 把 social 与 financial 拼成 "提高社会保障 金"，是基于熟词 social 的乱凑，原文从未提及社会保障金（social security 是美国福利 专名）。 文章关于从事体力劳动的人说了什么? A) 他们渴望退休后享受生活。 B) 他们可能会遇到财务困难。 C) 他们通常不喜欢做这种工作。 D) 他们倾向于期待退休。

questions.q: What does the passage say about people doing manual work?
options: They are eager to enjoy life after retiring.
They are likely to have financial troubles.
They generally don't enjoy doing it.
They tend to anticipate retirement.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the passage say about people doing manual work 直接问原文对该群 体的具体说法，按细节题处理。

【拆句】主干 What does the passage say about ...，about 引出对象；现在分词短语 doing manual work 后置修饰 people，相当于 who do manual work，无从句无难点。

【定位】Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons. 另一方面，从事体力劳动较多的工人则可能更期待退休；Baily 说，那些继续留下来的多半 是出于经济原因。

【选项】A) 过度推断 A 项 They are eager to enjoy life after retiring 把原文 "期待退休" 引申到 "渴望享受 退休后的生活"，原文只说期待退休、未提退休后做什么，引申了一步。 B) 过度推断 B 项 They are likely to have financial troubles 把原文 those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons 推到 "会陷入经济困境"，但 for financial reasons 只说 "出于经济原因"，不等同于 financial troubles。 C) 无中生有 C 项 They generally don't enjoy doing it 说 "他们通常不喜欢做这工作"，但原文只 说他们更期待退休、并未直接评价是否喜欢工作；不能由 "期待退休" 直接等同 "不喜欢 工作"。 D) ✓ 正确 may be more likely to look forward to retiring ↔They tend to anticipate retirement 预判抓 "期待退休"，D 项 They tend to anticipate retirement 是 look forward to retiring 的标准英英同义替换，选定无误。
